raw_evidence.quote: You can avoid repeating containers by creating nested maps.
Sometimes you want to reference something outside of the container from within. The underscore (`_`) refers to parent.

Can an object be part of more than 1 container?

...e.g., an item in the middle of a venn diagram.

Not currently and not in the near future.

multiple_logical_schemas_in_one_database.citation: docs/tour/containers.md, entire page — no 'schema' or 'namespace' keyword anywhere on the page; docs/tour/faq.md line 54-59 confirms a shape may belong to only one container
multiple_logical_schemas_in_one_database.rationale: D2's `container` primitive lets sql_table shapes be visually nested — e.g. a top-level `configuration: { ... }` container holding the TASK_VERSION and PLAN tables, alongside sibling `runtime: {}`, `audit: {}`, `resources: {}` containers — which would produce a diagram with four visually grouped clusters resembling four schemas. But the documentation attaches no schema-specific semantics to this: containers.md's own worked examples group cloud-provider resources (the generic 'gcloud: Google Cloud' example), not database schemas, and the page uses the identical primitive for any grouping purpose. There is no schema-qualified naming (e.g. no `configuration.task_version` cross-schema reference syntax distinct from ordinary nested-shape addressing), no schema-level constraint, and the FAQ confirms a shape can belong to only one container at a time with no near-term plan to change that — a stricter, purely-structural constraint, not a database-schema concept. Verdict: the visual grouping can be produced and would read correctly to a human, but it is a generic nesting primitive doing double duty, not a first-class schema/namespace construct — workaround, not genuine expressiveness.

cross_cutting_convention_assertable_by_v.citation: d2cli/validate.go (see companion record source-d2-sql-table-validation-exit.json) — validate performs syntax parsing only; GitHub issue-tracker search for lint/custom-rule terms returned no relevant results
cross_cutting_convention_assertable_by_v.rationale: There is no documented mechanism, built-in or plugin-based, for asserting a project-specific structural convention such as 'domain_id must be present on every Domain-owned sql_table' — this would require semantic knowledge of which tables are 'Domain-owned' and a rule engine to check column presence across many shapes, neither of which is implied by anything in D2's language reference, its validate command (confirmed syntax-only per the companion validation-exit record), or its issue tracker. No lint, plugin, or custom-rule-authoring mechanism was found. This would have to be implemented entirely outside D2, as an external script parsing the compiled diagram's shape data (e.g. via `d2 --to json` or similar, if such an export exists) — a workaround built OUTSIDE the tool, which the brief's own research question explicitly distinguishes from a built-in rule ('distinguishing a built-in rule from a workaround'). Since no external-inspection export format sufficient for this purpose was confirmed either, this is recorded as not-expressible rather than expressible-only-via-workaround.

contrary_evidence_search.result: No issue, discussion, or documentation page proposes or implements a cross-cutting structural-convention linter for D2 models; the only 'lint' hits in the repository concern the project's own Go/shell code-quality CI, unrelated to end-user diagram content. This is a corroborated negative finding, not merely an absence noticed once. Combined with the sql-table-shape record's search, the full set of open, primary-source-confirmed gaps against the advanced-construct checklist is: composite PK/FK (#671), multi-constraint-per-column ergonomics still evolving (#672, #1386), and general SQL-table-relationship rendering inconsistencies between engines (#2781) — all still open as of the 2026-08-14 search date, none contradicted by any closed/fixed issue found (the one closed pair, #1655/#1660, concerned a rendering bug for null constraints, not a capability gap).
